name: Ben Nevis
description: Ben Nevis is the highest mountain in the British Isles, standing at 1,345 meters above sea level. Located in the Scottish Highlands near Fort William, it attracts over 150,000 walkers annually.
history: The first recorded ascent was in 1771 by botanist James Robertson. The mountain's name comes from the Gaelic "Beinn Nibheis" meaning "malicious mountain" or "mountain with its head in the clouds". A meteorological observatory operated on the summit from 1883 to 1904.
fun_facts: Ben Nevis is the highest mountain in the British Isles
The summit plateau is the collapsed dome of an ancient volcano
Snow can remain on the mountain year-round
The famous Ben Nevis Race has been held since 1895
The first car was driven to the summit in 1911

name: Ben Macdui
description: Ben Macdui is the second highest mountain in the British Isles and the highest in the Cairngorms. At 1,309 meters, it offers spectacular views across the Cairngorm plateau.
history: The mountain is named after the Clan MacDuff. For many years, it was thought to be higher than Ben Nevis. The summit is home to legends of the "Big Grey Man" or "Fear Liath Mòr", a supernatural presence said to haunt the mountain.
fun_facts: Second highest mountain in Britain
Home to the legend of the Big Grey Man
Part of the Cairngorms plateau
Often climbed from Cairn Gorm ski area
Has a large summit cairn

name: Braeriach
description: Braeriach is the third highest mountain in the UK and the highest point in the western Cairngorms. Its vast summit plateau is home to arctic-alpine flora and one of Scotland's few permanent snowbeds.

name: Cairn Toul
description: Cairn Toul is the fourth highest mountain in Scotland, connected to Braeriach by a high col. The mountain offers spectacular views over the Lairig Ghru.

name: Sgor an Lochain Uaine
description: Also known as the Angel's Peak, this Munro is famous for its green lochan and dramatic cliffs. It's often climbed as part of a Cairngorms plateau traverse.

name: Cairn Gorm
description: Cairn Gorm gives its name to the Cairngorms mountain range and national park. The mountain is accessible via funicular railway, making it one of the most visited high peaks in Scotland.
history: The name means "Blue Hill" in Gaelic, referring to the blue-grey granite that forms the mountain. A ski resort has operated on its slopes since the 1960s, and the funicular railway opened in 2001.
fun_facts: Gave its name to the Cairngorms range
Home to Scotland's only funicular railway
Popular ski resort in winter
Summit plateau is arctic-alpine environment
One of five Scottish 4000-foot mountains

name: Aonach Beag
description: Despite its name meaning "little ridge", Aonach Beag is the seventh highest mountain in the British Isles at 1,234 meters. It sits in the shadow of its higher neighbor Aonach Mòr.
history: Aonach Beag is part of the Grey Corries range and offers some of the finest ridge walking in Scotland. The mountain is less frequently climbed than its neighbors despite its impressive height.
fun_facts: Seventh highest mountain in Britain despite name meaning "little ridge"
Offers spectacular ridge walking
Less crowded than nearby Ben Nevis
Part of the Grey Corries range
Usually climbed with Aonach Mòr

name: Aonach Mòr
description: Aonach Mòr is Scotland's eighth highest mountain. A ski resort operates on its slopes, and the Nevis Range gondola provides access to the mountain.

name: Carn Mòr Dearg
description: Famous for its knife-edge arête ridge, Carn Mòr Dearg is often climbed en route to Ben Nevis via the CMD Arête, one of Scotland's finest ridge walks.

name: Ben Lawers
description: Ben Lawers is the tenth highest mountain in Britain and the highest in the southern Highlands. It's famous for its arctic-alpine flora and was once thought to be Scotland's highest peak.

name: Beinn a' Bhuird
description: Beinn a' Bhuird has a massive plateau summit with huge granite cliffs on its northern face. It's one of the remotest Munros, requiring a long approach.

name: Lochnagar
description: Lochnagar is famous for its dramatic corrie and the dark lochan beneath its summit. The mountain has strong royal connections and inspired Lord Byron's poetry.

name: Bidean nam Bian
description: Bidean nam Bian is the highest peak in Argyll and the Glen Coe area. The mountain is hidden from the road by its three ridges, the Three Sisters of Glen Coe.

name: Ben Alder
description: Ben Alder is one of Scotland's most remote Munros, situated in wild country between Loch Ericht and Loch Laggan. The mountain has historical connections to Bonnie Prince Charlie.

name: Ben Cruachan
description: Ben Cruachan dominates the Pass of Brander and Loch Awe. The mountain has a vast horseshoe ridge and is home to the Cruachan Power Station hidden inside the mountain.

name: Stob Coire Easain
description: A fine Munro with excellent views, Stob Coire Easain is usually climbed with nearby Stob a' Choire Mheadhoin. The approach follows the West Highland Line railway.

name: Snowdon
description: Yr Wyddfa (Snowdon) is the highest mountain in Wales at 1,085 meters. Part of Snowdonia National Park, it can be reached by six different walking paths or the historic Snowdon Mountain Railway.
history: The Welsh name "Yr Wyddfa" means "the tumulus" or "the burial place". According to legend, the giant Rhita Gawr is buried at the summit. The mountain railway opened in 1896, making Snowdon one of the most accessible high peaks in Britain.
fun_facts: Highest mountain in Wales
Can be reached by mountain railway since 1896
Has six main walking paths to the summit
The summit visitor centre was redesigned and reopened in 2009
On a clear day, you can see Ireland, Scotland, England and the Isle of Man
facilities: Car parks at multiple starting points

name: Schiehallion
description: Schiehallion is one of Scotland's best-known mountains, famous for its near-perfect cone shape. It was used in 1774 for the first accurate measurement of Earth's mass.

name: Carnedd Llewelyn
description: Carnedd Llewelyn is the second highest mountain in Wales. The vast summit area is part of the wild Carneddau range, popular with wild campers.

name: An Teallach
description: An Teallach is considered one of Scotland's finest mountains, with a spectacular ridge featuring dramatic pinnacles. The traverse requires scrambling and a good head for heights.

name: Liathach
description: Liathach is one of the great Torridon mountains, with a terraced appearance and narrow ridge. The traverse is one of the finest mountain days in Scotland.

name: Carnedd Dafydd
description: Carnedd Dafydd is part of the main Carneddau ridge. The mountain is often climbed with Carnedd Llewelyn, forming a fine ridge walk.

name: Sgorr Dhearg
description: Part of the Beinn a' Bheithir ridge, Sgorr Dhearg offers stunning views over Loch Leven and Glen Coe. The ridge walk is airy and enjoyable.

name: Buachaille Etive Mòr
description: The "Great Herdsman of Etive" is one of Scotland's most iconic mountains, guarding the entrance to Glen Coe. Its pyramid shape is recognized worldwide.

name: Beinn Eighe
description: Beinn Eighe was Britain's first National Nature Reserve. The mountain has white quartzite screes and a long multi-topped ridge requiring careful navigation.

name: Glyder Fawr
description: Glyder Fawr is the highest of the Glyderau range. The summit area has bizarre rock formations, including Cantilever Stone, one of Wales' most photographed features.

name: Glyder Fach
description: Glyder Fach has a rocky summit with the famous Cantilever Stone. The summit castle of rocks provides shelter and excellent scrambling opportunities.

name: Sgurr Dearg
description: Sgurr Dearg is famous for the Inaccessible Pinnacle on its summit, a vertical rock tower requiring rock climbing skills. It's the only Munro that must be climbed rather than walked.

name: Scafell Pike
description: Scafell Pike is the highest mountain in England at 978 meters. Located in the Lake District National Park, it forms part of the famous Three Peaks Challenge along with Ben Nevis and Snowdon.
history: The mountain takes its name from the Old Norse "Skalfjall" meaning "bald mountain". The summit was gifted to the National Trust in 1919 as a memorial to the men of the Lake District who died in World War I.
fun_facts: Highest peak in England
Part of the National Three Peaks Challenge
The first recorded ascent was by Samuel Taylor Coleridge in 1802
Named after the Old Norse for "bald mountain"
Over 250,000 people climb it each year

name: Ben Lomond
description: Ben Lomond is one of Scotland's most popular Munros, offering stunning views over Loch Lomond and the Trossachs. Its accessibility from Glasgow makes it a favorite for day hikes.
history: The name comes from the Gaelic "Beinn Laomainn" meaning "beacon mountain". It has been a popular climbing destination since the 18th century and was one of the first Munros many climbers ascend.
fun_facts: One of the most southerly Munros
Most popular Munro in Scotland by number of ascents
Owned and managed by the National Trust for Scotland
Takes about 6-7 hours for the round trip
Forms part of the Loch Lomond and The Trossachs National Park

name: Sgurr nan Gillean
description: Sgurr nan Gillean is one of the Black Cuillin peaks on Skye. The mountain requires scrambling and rock climbing skills, offering spectacular views over the island.

name: Helvellyn
description: Helvellyn is the third highest peak in England and one of the most popular mountains in the Lake District. The mountain offers several challenging routes including the famous Striding Edge.
history: The mountain has been a popular destination since the 18th century. In 1926, an aircraft landed on the summit plateau, and a memorial stone commemorates this event. The name possibly derives from the Celtic "hal" meaning moorland.
fun_facts: Third highest mountain in England
Features the famous Striding Edge ridge walk
An airplane landed on the summit in 1926
Can be climbed year-round but requires winter skills in cold months
Over 250,000 walkers climb it annually
facilities: Car parks at Glenridding and Patterdale

name: Sgurr Mhic Choinnich
description: One of the Black Cuillin peaks, Sgurr Mhic Choinnich is a rocky summit requiring scrambling. The peak is often climbed as part of the Cuillin Ridge traverse.

name: Y Garn
description: Y Garn overlooks Llyn Ogwen and has a distinctive pyramidal shape. The Devil's Kitchen cleft on the northeast face is a famous climbing venue.

name: Ill Crag
description: Ill Crag is part of the Scafell massif and England's third highest peak. It's usually climbed as part of a round from Wasdale or Borrowdale.

name: Skiddaw
description: Skiddaw is one of the Lake District's most prominent mountains and one of the easiest to climb. The mountain overlooks Keswick and Derwentwater.

name: Beinn Liath Mhòr
description: A sprawling Corbett in the Fannichs with a long summit ridge. The mountain offers good views of the surrounding peaks and is usually climbed from Glen Fannich.

name: Elidir Fawr
description: Elidir Fawr is the northernmost of the major Snowdonia peaks. Inside the mountain is the Dinorwig Power Station, a massive pumped-storage facility.

name: Crib Goch
description: Crib Goch is the most famous knife-edge ridge in Wales. The exposed scramble is the classic route up Snowdon but requires a good head for heights.

name: Tryfan
description: Tryfan is one of Wales' most famous mountains, requiring scrambling to reach the summit. Adam and Eve, two monoliths on the summit, are traditionally jumped between.

name: Beinn Dearg
description: A magnificent Corbett in Torridon with superb views of the main Torridon peaks. The mountain offers a rewarding day out with less crowds than the nearby Munros.

name: Foinaven
description: Foinaven is a remote and spectacular mountain in Sutherland, featuring white quartzite screes and dramatic corries. The mountain requires a long approach through wild country.

name: Great End
description: Great End is at the head of Borrowdale with impressive crags. Often climbed with Scafell Pike, it gives spectacular views down the valley.

name: Aran Fawddwy
description: Aran Fawddwy is the highest peak in the Aran range and southern Snowdonia. The mountain is more remote and less visited than the northern peaks.

name: Bowfell
description: Bowfell is a beautiful mountain at the head of Langdale. The summit is a rocky pyramid with excellent views, and the route via The Band is classic.

name: Great Gable
description: Great Gable is one of the Lake District's most iconic mountains. Its distinctive shape dominates the head of Wasdale, and it was gifted to the National Trust as a war memorial.

name: Cadair Idris
description: Cadair Idris is one of the most famous mountains in Wales. Legend says anyone who spends the night on its summit will awaken either a poet or a madman.
history: The name means "Chair of Idris" in Welsh, referring to a giant from Welsh mythology. The mountain has been a tourist destination since Victorian times and inspired many poets and artists including Richard Wilson and J.M.W. Turner.
fun_facts: Name means "Chair of Idris" in Welsh mythology
Legend says sleeping on the summit makes you a poet or madman
Has three main walking routes
Popular with Victorian tourists and artists
Home to rare arctic-alpine plants

name: Pillar
description: Pillar is one of the great Lake District mountains, with the famous Pillar Rock on its northern face. The summit gives excellent views of the western fells.

name: Pen y Fan
description: Pen y Fan is the highest peak in South Wales and southern Britain. Part of the Brecon Beacons, it features distinctive flat-topped summit and is visible for miles around.
history: The name means "top of the place" or "highest point" in Welsh. The mountain is used by the military for training, including the SAS selection process. The Roman road Sarn Helen passes nearby.
fun_facts: Highest peak in southern Britain
Most climbed mountain in Wales
Distinctive flat-topped summit
Used for SAS selection training
Can be climbed year-round
facilities: Car park at Pont ar Daf
restaurants: Storey Arms Outdoor Education Centre Cafe

name: Fairfield
description: Fairfield is the highest point of the popular Fairfield Horseshoe walk from Ambleside. The mountain has a broad summit plateau.

name: Corn Du
description: Corn Du is the twin summit of Pen y Fan, separated by a small col. The two are usually climbed together on the most popular route in the Brecon Beacons.

name: Moel Siabod
description: Moel Siabod is an isolated peak offering superb views of Snowdon. The mountain is easily accessible from Capel Curig and provides excellent walking.

name: Blencathra
description: Blencathra, also known as Saddleback, has several ridges offering varied routes. Sharp Edge provides one of the Lake District's finest scrambles.

name: Crinkle Crags
description: Crinkle Crags is a mountain with five main "crinkles" or summits. The route involves scrambling and is one of Lakeland's finest ridge walks.

name: Grasmoor
description: Grasmoor is the highest of the northwestern fells. The mountain has steep sides, particularly Dove Crags, and commands excellent views.

name: Cul Mor
description: Cul Mor is the highest of the Assynt Corbetts. The approach passes spectacular sandstone scenery, and the summit gives panoramic views.

name: High Street
description: High Street follows a Roman road and has one of the Lake District's longest summit ridges. The mountain offers easy walking with extensive views.

name: Quinag
description: Quinag is a complex mountain with three main tops. The Y-shaped ridge offers superb walking with dramatic views over the Assynt landscape.

name: Coniston Old Man
description: Coniston Old Man towers over the village of Coniston and its lake. Mining remains on its slopes tell of its industrial past, while the summit gives superb views.

name: Cribyn
description: Cribyn has a sharp pointed summit and is often climbed with Pen y Fan. The mountain forms part of the classic Brecon Beacons horseshoe walk.

name: Cul Beag
description: Cul Beag is smaller than its neighbor Cul Mor but offers equally fine views. The mountain has dramatic cliffs on its northern side.

name: Ben Loyal
description: Known as the "Queen of Scottish Mountains", Ben Loyal has four distinctive peaks. The mountain dominates the landscape of northwest Sutherland.

name: Ben More Coigach
description: Ben More Coigach is a remote mountain accessed via a long walk through the Coigach hills. The summit provides spectacular views over the Summer Isles.

name: Whernside
description: Whernside is the highest of the Yorkshire Three Peaks. The walk along the ridge from Ribblehead Viaduct is spectacular, with panoramic views.

name: Fan Fawr
description: Fan Fawr is in the western Brecon Beacons. The mountain has a distinctive shape and offers good walking with less crowds than Pen y Fan.

name: Ingleborough
description: Ingleborough has a distinctive flat summit plateau that was once an Iron Age hill fort. It's the second peak in the Yorkshire Three Peaks challenge.

name: Ben Stack
description: Ben Stack is an isolated peak with superb views over numerous lochs and to the mountains of Sutherland. The ascent is straightforward but rewarding.

name: Kinder Scout
description: Kinder Scout is the highest point in the Peak District. The plateau is famous for the Mass Trespass of 1932, a pivotal moment in the campaign for access to open country.

name: Bleaklow
description: Bleaklow is a wild peat moorland plateau. The summit area can be boggy, but the walk offers solitude and great views over the Dark Peak.

name: Stac Pollaidh
description: Despite its modest height, Stac Pollaidh is one of Scotland's most distinctive peaks. The sandstone pinnacles and scrambling opportunities make it extremely popular.

name: Haystacks
description: Despite its modest height, Haystacks was Alfred Wainwright's favorite mountain. His ashes were scattered here, and the summit overlooks Innominate Tarn.
